# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

# Every gate this project enforces. Contributors can reproduce all of them
# locally; see CONTRIBUTING.md for the equivalent npm commands. Releases are
# handled separately, by release.yml.
#
# `internal-ref-scan` below checks a public-safe subset of patterns. A few
# internal patterns are credential-shaped and are deliberately not committed
# here as literals: writing them into a public repo would defeat the point of
# scanning for them.
name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  # Callable so release.yml can run this exact workflow against a tagged
  # commit, making the release gate and the pull-request gate the same object
  # instead of two lists somebody has to keep in step by hand. They had
  # already drifted: release.yml ran six of these jobs while describing itself
  # as "the full gate".
  #
  # dco-check and commitlint-check are guarded by
  # `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` and skip when called, because a
  # reusable workflow sees the *caller's* event. On a release that is the tag
  # push, and neither check is meaningful against a tag.
  workflow_call:

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

# Least privilege: no job in this workflow writes to the repo. Anything that
# needs more must elevate explicitly at the job level.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: ".nvmrc"
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci --prefer-offline
      - run: npm run build
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: dist
          path: packages/*/dist
          retention-days: 1

  lint-format:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: ".nvmrc"
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci --prefer-offline
      - run: npx biome check .

  typecheck:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    needs: build
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: ".nvmrc"
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci --prefer-offline
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: dist
          path: packages
      - run: npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json

  license-headers:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: ".nvmrc"
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci --prefer-offline
      - run: node ./scripts/verify-license-headers.mjs

  reuse-lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: fsfe/reuse-action@676e2d560c9a403aa252096d99fcab3e1132b0f5 # v6.0.0

  # Also proves THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES isn't stale: verify:packaging must run
  # FIRST against the committed files, then generate-notices regenerates
  # them, then the diff must be empty. Reversing the order would validate
  # freshly written files instead of committed ones and make this a
  # tautology.
  verify-packaging:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: ".nvmrc"
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci --prefer-offline
      - run: npm run verify:packaging
      - run: npm run generate-notices
      - run: |
          git diff --exit-code -- THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES 'packages/*/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES' || {
            echo "FAIL: THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES is stale: run 'npm run generate-notices' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          }

  # There is deliberately no `license-check` job here. One existed, running
  # `npx license-checker --production`, and it asserted nothing: no manifest in
  # this repo declares runtime dependencies, so `--production` narrowed the
  # tree to the root package (which the job then excluded by name) plus the
  # four first-party workspaces. There was no third-party license for it to
  # fail on, and by design there never will be. It also reached the network for
  # an unpinned tool on every run, in a pipeline that otherwise resolves
  # everything from the lockfile or a commit SHA.
  #
  # What that job was reaching for is now asserted directly, offline, by
  # verify-packaging (see the FORBIDDEN_DEP_FIELDS check in
  # scripts/verify-packaging.mjs): the published packages declare no runtime
  # dependencies at all, which is the claim THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES makes and the
  # stronger of the two guarantees. Adding a runtime dependency fails that gate
  # and forces the notices to be updated in the same change.
  #
  # Note this covers *runtime* licensing only. devDependency licenses are not
  # scanned by anything here, on the grounds that build-time tooling is not
  # distributed in the tarballs. If that policy changes, a license scanner
  # belongs in root devDependencies, not behind `npx`.

  # Supported-Node matrix: proves the toolchain and tests actually RUN on
  # every Node line the published `engines.node` (">=22") claims to support,
  # not just the single version (.nvmrc) every other job is pinned to.
  #
  # Deliberately self-contained (no artifacts in or out) rather than
  # matrixing `build`/`typecheck`/etc: those jobs share a `dist` artifact
  # under a fixed name, and `upload-artifact@v4` errors on duplicate names;
  # matrixing `build` would collide. What this job needs to prove, that
  # build/typecheck/test/pack all RUN on both lines, is fully exercised by
  # its own from-scratch install+build. What genuinely isn't Node-sensitive
  # (grep/fs/JSON.parse jobs like bundle-treeshake, cdn-free,
  # verify-packaging) deliberately stays single-version.
  node-matrix:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 25
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        node: ["22", "24"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci --prefer-offline
      - run: npm run build
      - run: npm run typecheck
      - run: npm run test
      - run: npm run test:react-compat
      # Tree-shake boundary, mirrored from bundle-treeshake below, so it's
      # proven on both supported Node lines and not just the pinned default.
      # Unlike that job's `grep -l ... 2>/dev/null`, this asserts the file
      # exists first: a missing dist file must FAIL, not silently pass.
      - run: |
          set -e
          for f in packages/react-gui-icons/dist/icons/Gpu.mjs \
                   packages/react-micro-gui-icons/dist/icons/Add.mjs; do
            test -f "$f" || { echo "FAIL: $f not built"; exit 1; }
            ! grep -q "inlineMap" "$f" || { echo "FAIL: $f references inlineMap: tree-shaking boundary broken"; exit 1; }
            echo "✓ Tree-shake test passed: $f does not reference inlineMap"
          done

  react-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    needs: build
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: ".nvmrc"
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci --prefer-offline
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: dist
          path: packages
      - run: npm run test -w @nvidia/react-gui-icons
      - run: npm run test -w @nvidia/react-micro-gui-icons
      - run: npm run test:react-compat

  pack-smoke:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    needs: build
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: ".nvmrc"
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci --prefer-offline
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: dist
          path: packages
      - run: |
          fail=0
          for pkg in gui-icons micro-gui-icons react-gui-icons react-micro-gui-icons; do
            dir="packages/$pkg"
            echo "── $pkg ──"
            # npm pack's tarball listing has an occasional, narrowly-scoped
            # flake on this runner class: a files-array-only entry (NOTICE or
            # THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES) is absent from an otherwise-successful
            # pack, while LICENSE (always-included by npm via a separate
            # code path, not the files-array walk) never drops. Not
            # reproducible locally, and not something we can pin our way out
            # of from this repo. Retry the whole pack+verify a few times
            # before treating it as a real defect, rather than failing the
            # pipeline on tool flakiness; a genuine regression fails every
            # attempt identically, so this can't mask one.
            attempt=1
            max_attempts=3
            pkg_ok=0
            while [ "$attempt" -le "$max_attempts" ]; do
              pkg_fail=0
              packdir=$(mktemp -d)
              (cd "$dir" && npm pack --pack-destination "$packdir" >/dev/null 2>&1)
              tgz=$(echo "$packdir"/*.tgz)
              files=$(tar -tzf "$tgz")
              for required in LICENSE NOTICE THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES; do
                echo "$files" | grep -q "package/$required" || { echo "MISSING: $required in $pkg (attempt $attempt/$max_attempts)"; pkg_fail=1; }
              done
              echo "$files" | grep -q 'package/dist/' || { echo "MISSING: dist/ in $pkg (attempt $attempt/$max_attempts)"; pkg_fail=1; }
              if echo "$pkg" | grep -qv "^react-"; then
                echo "$files" | grep -q 'package/assets/' || { echo "MISSING: assets/ in $pkg (attempt $attempt/$max_attempts)"; pkg_fail=1; }
              fi
              license_body=$(tar -xzOf "$tgz" package/LICENSE 2>/dev/null)
              echo "$license_body" | grep -q "Apache License" \
                || { echo "MISSING: Apache-2.0 text in $pkg LICENSE (attempt $attempt/$max_attempts)"; pkg_fail=1; }
              echo "$license_body" | grep -q "Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International" \
                || { echo "MISSING: CC-BY-4.0 text in $pkg LICENSE (attempt $attempt/$max_attempts)"; pkg_fail=1; }
              if echo "$license_body" | grep -qi "provisional"; then
                echo "STALE: provisional stub LICENSE in $pkg"; pkg_fail=1
              fi
              license_field=$(tar -xzOf "$tgz" package/package.json 2>/dev/null | node -e "
                const chunks=[]; process.stdin.on('data',c=>chunks.push(c));
                process.stdin.on('end',()=>{
                  process.stdout.write(String(JSON.parse(chunks.join('')).license || ''));
                });
              ")
              if [ "$license_field" != "CC-BY-4.0 AND Apache-2.0" ]; then
                echo "WRONG: $pkg package.json license is '$license_field'"; pkg_fail=1
              fi
              rm -rf "$packdir"
              if [ "$pkg_fail" -eq 0 ]; then
                pkg_ok=1
                break
              fi
              attempt=$((attempt + 1))
              [ "$attempt" -le "$max_attempts" ] && sleep 2
            done
            if [ "$pkg_ok" -eq 1 ]; then
              if [ "$attempt" -gt 1 ]; then
                echo "  ✓ $pkg pack contents validated (recovered after retry $((attempt - 1)))"
              else
                echo "  ✓ $pkg pack contents validated"
              fi
            else
              echo "  ✗ $pkg pack contents FAILED after $max_attempts attempts"
              fail=1
            fi
          done
          exit $fail

  bundle-treeshake:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    needs: build
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: dist
          path: packages
      # Assert each file exists before grepping it. Writing this as
      # `if grep -l ... 2>/dev/null` passes silently on a missing file: grep
      # exits 2, the redirect hides the error, and `if` reads non-zero as
      # "no match". `set -e` does not catch it either, because the failure is
      # inside an `if` condition. Same guard as node-matrix above.
      - run: |
          set -e
          for f in packages/react-gui-icons/dist/icons/Gpu.mjs \
                   packages/react-micro-gui-icons/dist/icons/Add.mjs; do
            test -f "$f" || { echo "FAIL: $f not built"; exit 1; }
            ! grep -q "inlineMap" "$f" || { echo "FAIL: $f references inlineMap: tree-shaking boundary broken"; exit 1; }
            echo "✓ Tree-shake test passed: $f does not reference inlineMap"
          done

  cdn-free:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - run: |
          set -e
          fail=0
          for pkg in react-gui-icons react-micro-gui-icons; do
            echo "── $pkg ──"
            # Assert the scan targets exist first. `if grep ... ; then` on a
            # missing path passes silently: grep exits 2, `if` reads non-zero
            # as "no match", and `set -e` does not fire inside an `if`
            # condition. A renamed package would otherwise report "CDN-free
            # check passed" having scanned nothing. Same guard as
            # bundle-treeshake and internal-ref-scan.
            pkg_fail=0
            for target in "packages/$pkg" "packages/$pkg/src"; do
              if [ ! -d "$target" ]; then
                echo "FAIL: scan target '$target' does not exist"; pkg_fail=1
              fi
            done
            # Missing directory: record it and move to the next package rather
            # than grepping a path that isn't there. Per-package flag, so one
            # package failing never truncates the scan of the next.
            if [ "$pkg_fail" -eq 1 ]; then fail=1; continue; fi
            if grep -rn "external-svg-loader" "packages/$pkg/"; then
              echo "FAIL: $pkg references external-svg-loader"; pkg_fail=1
            fi
            if grep -rn 'data-src=' "packages/$pkg/src/"; then
              echo "FAIL: $pkg uses data-src (CDN loader placeholder)"; pkg_fail=1
            fi
            if grep -rn 'cne\.ngc\.nvidia\.com' "packages/$pkg/"; then
              echo "FAIL: $pkg references CDN host"; pkg_fail=1
            fi
            if [ "$pkg_fail" -eq 0 ]; then
              echo "  ✓ $pkg CDN-free check passed"
            else
              fail=1
            fi
          done
          exit $fail

  sbom:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: ".nvmrc"
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci --prefer-offline
      - run: |
          # Pinned to an exact npm 11.x release rather than the npm bundled
          # with the pinned Node image or `@latest`: `npm sbom` needs npm
          # >= 11.5, the bundled npm for a given Node image isn't guaranteed
          # to clear that floor, and `@latest` would drift the tool version
          # between runs. 11.19.0 is the newest 11.x release.
          npm install -g npm@11.19.0
          mkdir -p sbom
          for pkg in gui-icons micro-gui-icons react-gui-icons react-micro-gui-icons; do
            npm sbom -w "packages/$pkg" --sbom-format cyclonedx > "sbom/$pkg.cdx.json"
          done
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: sbom
          path: sbom/
          retention-days: 90

  # Internal-reference scan (public-safe subset): checks for internal
  # hostnames/scopes/codenames that shouldn't appear in a public repo. A
  # smaller set of sensitive, credential-shaped patterns is deliberately not
  # committed here; see the note at the top of this file.
  internal-ref-scan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - run: |
          set -e
          fail=0
          # CUTOVER.md was the internal migration runbook for this repo's
          # move to GitHub. It is deleted, and must never reappear in a
          # public tree. Checked explicitly rather than relying only on the
          # pattern scan below, since presence, not content, is the actual
          # condition to catch.
          if [ -e CUTOVER.md ]; then
            echo "FAIL internal-ref-scan: CUTOVER.md is present. It is an internal-only migration document and must not exist in this repository."
            fail=1
          fi
          patterns=(
            "git"'lab-master\.nvidia\.com'
            # Any reference to the internal instance or its config files.
            # `.github/` is a scan target, so a ported comment mentioning it
            # is exactly the kind of leak this catches.
            "[Gg]it"'[Ll]ab'
            "urm\.nvidia\.com"
            "brand-assets\.cne\.ngc\.nvidia\.com"
            # Split across a quote boundary so this job's own source doesn't
            # contain the literal substring it's scanning for. Needed now
            # that .github/ itself is a scan target below.
            "@nv-brand"'-assets/'
            "sw-nvpubcloud"'-npm-local'
            "sw-ngc-unified"'-npm-proxy'
            "nvidia\.slack\.com"
            "nvbugs"'/'
            "confluence\.nvidia\.com"
            # Internal NVIDIA process jargon (OSS Review Board, System
            # Architecture Design Doc) that means nothing to an external
            # contributor if it leaks into a shipped comment or error message.
            '\b[Oo][Ss][Rr][Bb]\b'
            '\b[Ss][Aa][Dd][Dd]\b'
          )
          scan_dirs=(
            packages/ scripts/
            README.md CONTRIBUTING.md SECURITY.md CHANGELOG.md CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
            GOVERNANCE.md MAINTAINERS.md SUPPORT.md RELEASING.md
            CODEOWNERS NOTICE THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES LICENSE REUSE.toml package.json
            package-lock.json
            .github/ .well-known/ LICENSES/
          )
          # Fail loudly on a missing scan target instead of letting grep's
          # error (exit 2) get swallowed by `2>/dev/null || true` below: a
          # stale or typo'd entry must not silently degrade to "scanned
          # nothing" with a green check. CUTOVER.md is deliberately NOT in
          # this "must exist" list; its absence is the desired state
          # (checked explicitly above); it's only added to the grep targets
          # below, as defense-in-depth in case it exists but wasn't caught by
          # the explicit check for some reason.
          for scan_dir in "${scan_dirs[@]}"; do
            if [ ! -e "$scan_dir" ]; then
              echo "FAIL internal-ref-scan: scan target '$scan_dir' does not exist"
              fail=1
            fi
          done
          # Second, separate trap: grep's --include filters by basename glob,
          # and that filter also applies to files named explicitly on the
          # command line (verified against GNU grep 3.12, what this runner
          # ships), not just to files discovered by recursing into a
          # directory. A scan target whose basename matches none of the globs
          # below is silently read as zero bytes: the existence check above
          # still passes, the pattern loop finds nothing, and the job goes
          # green having scanned nothing. Keep this case pattern in sync with
          # the --include flags in the grep call below.
          for scan_dir in "${scan_dirs[@]}" CUTOVER.md; do
            case "$scan_dir" in
              */) continue ;; # directories are exempt: recursion applies filters per-file, not to the dir arg itself
            esac
            base="$(basename "$scan_dir")"
            case "$base" in
              *.ts|*.tsx|*.mts|*.js|*.mjs|*.json|*.md|*.yml|*.yaml|*.toml|*.txt|CODEOWNERS|NOTICE|THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES|LICENSE) ;;
              *)
                echo "FAIL internal-ref-scan: scan target '$scan_dir' matches no --include glob: grep would silently skip it"
                fail=1
                ;;
            esac
          done
          if [ "$fail" -eq 1 ]; then exit 1; fi
          grep_targets=("${scan_dirs[@]}" CUTOVER.md)
          for pattern in "${patterns[@]}"; do
            matches=$(grep -rn --include="*.ts" --include="*.tsx" --include="*.mts" \
              --include="*.js" --include="*.mjs" --include="*.json" \
              --include="*.md" --include="*.yml" --include="*.yaml" \
              --include="*.toml" --include="*.txt" \
              --include="CODEOWNERS" --include="NOTICE" --include="THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES" \
              --include="LICENSE" \
              -E "$pattern" "${grep_targets[@]}" \
              --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=dist \
              2>/dev/null || true)
            if [ -n "$matches" ]; then
              echo "FAIL internal-ref-scan: pattern '$pattern' matched:"
              echo "$matches"
              fail=1
            fi
          done
          if [ $fail -eq 0 ]; then echo "✓ No internal references found."; fi
          exit $fail

  dco-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0
      # Uses the event payload's base SHA rather than `origin/$base_ref`. On a
      # pull_request event, checkout lands on a detached merge ref and
      # `origin/main` isn't guaranteed to be a resolvable local ref: that
      # would either fail every PR or mis-scope the commit range. The base SHA
      # is always present in the payload and needs no ref resolution.
      #
      # BASE_SHA/HEAD_SHA go through `env:` instead of being interpolated
      # straight into the script, so the values are never expanded into shell
      # source text.
      - env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          set -e
          missing=""
          for sha in $(git log --format=%H "$BASE_SHA".."$HEAD_SHA"); do
            if ! git log --format=%B -1 "$sha" | grep -q "^Signed-off-by:"; then
              missing="$missing$sha $(git log --format=%s -1 "$sha")\n"
            fi
          done
          if [ -n "$missing" ]; then
            echo "FAIL: the following commits are missing Signed-off-by trailers:"
            printf "%b" "$missing"
            echo "Add with: git commit --signoff"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "✓ All commits have Signed-off-by trailers."

  # husky's commit-msg hook (`.husky/commit-msg`) gives fast local feedback,
  # but it only fires for contributors who ran `npm install` (which runs the
  # `prepare` script). It's trivially skippable with `--no-verify` and never
  # runs at all for edits made through the GitHub web UI. This job is the
  # actual gate: same commitlint config, same conventional-commits rule set,
  # run here so it can't be bypassed.
  commitlint-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: ".nvmrc"
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci --prefer-offline
      # Same BASE_SHA/HEAD_SHA-via-env pattern as dco-check above, and the
      # same reasoning for why it's the payload SHAs and not `origin/$ref`.
      - env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: npx commitlint --from "$BASE_SHA" --to "$HEAD_SHA" --verbose

# Publishes the four @nvidia icon packages to the public npm registry.
#
# Auth is npm Trusted Publishing (OIDC): there is no NPM_TOKEN anywhere in
# this file. Setup, the one-time bootstrap each package needs before its
# first release, and the step ordering that provenance depends on are all
# documented in RELEASING.md. Read that before cutting a release.
name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*.*.*"]

# Never cancel an in-flight release: a half-cancelled run can leave some
# packages published and others not. CI's cancel-in-progress is right for PRs
# and wrong here.
concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  # Cheap guard, run before the full suite so that a tag pointing somewhere it
  # should not is rejected in seconds rather than after a complete build and
  # test matrix has been spent on it.
  #
  # Split out of `verify` because that job is now a call into ci.yml and can no
  # longer carry a release-specific step.
  tag-guard:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          # Needed for merge-base: the check is meaningless against a shallow
          # clone that does not contain the commits it has to compare.
          fetch-depth: 0

      # Refuse to publish a tag that is not an ancestor of main. Without this,
      # anyone able to push a tag could publish an unreviewed branch to npm
      # under the NVIDIA scope.
      - name: Tag must be reachable from main
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git fetch --no-tags origin main
          if ! git merge-base --is-ancestor "$GITHUB_SHA" origin/main; then
            echo "FAIL: tagged commit $GITHUB_SHA is not an ancestor of origin/main."
            echo "Releases must be cut from reviewed, merged commits."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "✓ tagged commit is on main"

  # The full CI suite, re-run against the tagged commit. CI already ran it when
  # the commit landed on main, but a tag can point anywhere, and "it passed on
  # main" is not the same claim as "it passes at the thing we are about to
  # publish".
  #
  # `uses:` rather than a copy of the commands, because the copy drifted. This
  # job used to run build, lint, typecheck, test, test:react-compat and
  # verify:packaging, and call itself "the full gate", while ci.yml had grown
  # pack-smoke, bundle-treeshake, cdn-free, sbom, node-matrix (22 and 24),
  # reuse-lint, license-headers, internal-ref-scan and a THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES
  # drift check. The tarball smoke test and the Node 22 matrix are the two most
  # release-relevant of those, and neither had ever run against a commit that
  # was published. A call cannot drift.
  #
  # ci.yml carries its own `concurrency` with cancel-in-progress, so pushing
  # the same tag twice cancels the first run's verify. That is the desired
  # outcome and it is safe: nothing has been published at this point.
  verify:
    needs: tag-guard
    uses: ./.github/workflows/ci.yml

  publish:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 25
    needs: verify
    # Human approval gate. Must match the environment registered with the
    # trusted publisher on npmjs.com. See RELEASING.md.
    environment: npm-publish
    # Consumed by github-release below, so it can name the packages without
    # re-deriving which ones matched the tag. Two copies of that rule would
    # drift, and the copy that drifts is the one nobody runs on every release.
    outputs:
      packages: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.packages }}
    permissions:
      contents: read
      # The entire auth configuration. Without this the OIDC token cannot be
      # requested and both the publish and its provenance fail.
      id-token: write
    steps:
      # Pinned to the immutable SHA that triggered this run, not the tag ref.
      # This job waits on environment approval, which can take hours, and a
      # tag is mutable: a force-push in that window would otherwise mean the
      # commit published here is not the commit `verify` approved.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: ".nvmrc"
          cache: npm
      # Deliberately NOT using setup-node's `registry-url`: it writes an
      # `_authToken=${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}` line into .npmrc, which is pointless
      # with no token and risks an empty-credential line. The repo's own
      # .npmrc already pins registry.npmjs.org, which is what matters; a
      # machine with internal Artifactory config in its user-level .npmrc
      # resolves to the wrong registry otherwise.
      - run: npm ci --prefer-offline

      # npm's own docs disagree on the trusted-publishing floor: the
      # overview says >= 11.5.1, the npm-trust CLI reference says >= 11.15.0.
      # 11.19.0 clears both. Provenance's floor is much older (9.5.0) and is
      # not the binding constraint. Trusted publishing also wants Node >=
      # 22.14.0; .nvmrc pins 24, so that holds, but lowering .nvmrc into an
      # early 22.x would break releases. Pinned to an exact release rather
      # than @latest or the Node image's bundled npm, for the same reason the
      # sbom job pins it: reproducible tooling for a release-signing step.
      - run: npm install -g npm@11.19.0

      # Version guard. The tag is the release's claim about what is being
      # shipped; the manifests are the truth. If they disagree, stop.
      #
      # Packages version independently (see CONTRIBUTING.md), so this does NOT
      # require all four to sit at the tag version: it publishes exactly
      # those that do, and skips the rest loudly. What it refuses to do is
      # proceed when NOTHING matches, which is the typo'd-tag case that would
      # otherwise "succeed" having published nothing at all.
      - name: Resolve packages to publish
        id: resolve
        env:
          TAG_NAME: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          tag_version="${TAG_NAME#v}"
          echo "Tag $TAG_NAME -> version $tag_version"
          matched=""
          skipped=""
          # Dependency order: the base packages precede the React packages
          # that depend on them, so a consumer never sees a react-* package
          # whose dependency is not yet resolvable on the registry.
          for pkg in gui-icons micro-gui-icons react-gui-icons react-micro-gui-icons; do
            manifest="packages/$pkg/package.json"
            name=$(node -p "require('./$manifest').name")
            version=$(node -p "require('./$manifest').version")
            private=$(node -p "String(require('./$manifest').private === true)")
            if [ "$private" = "true" ]; then
              skipped="$skipped  - $name (private: true)"$'\n'
              continue
            fi
            if [ "$version" != "$tag_version" ]; then
              skipped="$skipped  - $name@$version (does not match tag $tag_version)"$'\n'
              continue
            fi
            matched="$matched$pkg"$'\n'
          done
          echo "Will publish:"
          if [ -n "$matched" ]; then printf '%s' "$matched"; else echo "  (none)"; fi
          if [ -n "$skipped" ]; then echo "Skipping:"; printf '%s' "$skipped"; fi
          if [ -z "$matched" ]; then
            echo "FAIL: no package version matches tag $tag_version: nothing to publish."
            echo "Either the tag is wrong or the version bump was never committed."
            exit 1
          fi
          printf '%s' "$matched" > /tmp/to-publish.txt
          # Same list, flattened onto one line, for the github-release job.
          # Safe as a plain (non-heredoc) GITHUB_OUTPUT assignment only
          # because every element is a directory name drawn from the literal
          # list above: no newlines, no user-controlled content.
          printf 'packages=%s\n' "$(printf '%s' "$matched" | tr '\n' ' ')" \
            >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Publish
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          fail=0
          while read -r pkg; do
            [ -n "$pkg" ] || continue
            manifest="packages/$pkg/package.json"
            name=$(node -p "require('./$manifest').name")
            version=$(node -p "require('./$manifest').version")
            echo "── $name@$version"
            # Idempotence: a run that dies partway through (network, approval
            # timeout) must be safe to re-run. npm would reject the already
            # published ones with a hard error and abort the whole release,
            # so skip what is already on the registry instead.
            if npm view "$name@$version" version >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "   already on registry, skipping"
              continue
            fi
            # Dist-tag. npm defaults an untagged publish to `latest`, which
            # is correct for a GA version but would clobber `latest` with a
            # prerelease: packages version independently and prereleases
            # are a first-class part of the release cadence driven by the
            # upstream sync generator, so a `-rc.1`/`-beta.2`/etc tag here
            # must land on `next`, never `latest`.
            if [[ "$version" == *-* ]]; then dist_tag="next"; else dist_tag="latest"; fi
            echo "   dist-tag: $dist_tag"
            # --provenance is redundant under trusted publishing, which turns
            # it on by default. Passed explicitly anyway so that a broken OIDC
            # setup FAILS here rather than silently publishing an unattested
            # tarball that nobody notices until an audit.
            # `npm publish <path>` is NOT a folder publish: npm resolves a
            # bare `a/b` argument as a GitHub owner/repo git spec, not a
            # directory, so this would fetch github.com/packages/<pkg> and
            # publish THAT under the @nvidia scope, provenance and all.
            # Publish from inside the directory, with no spec argument at all.
            (cd "packages/$pkg" && npm publish --access public --provenance --tag "$dist_tag") \
              || { echo "   FAILED"; fail=1; break; }
            echo "   ✓ published"
          done < /tmp/to-publish.txt
          exit $fail

  # The human-readable half of a release. A tag on its own tells a reader
  # nothing about what changed, and npm's page shows one package at a time
  # while a tag here can cover several.
  #
  # A separate job rather than a step on `publish`, because the two need
  # different and non-overlapping write permissions: `publish` holds
  # `id-token: write` to mint the OIDC credential npm trusts, this one holds
  # `contents: write` to create a release. Granting both to one job would mean
  # the job that can publish under the @nvidia scope can also rewrite the
  # repository it claims to be publishing from.
  #
  # No `environment:` on purpose. `needs: publish` means the npm-publish
  # reviewer gate has already been passed; a second approval prompt to write
  # notes about a publish that has already happened would only train reviewers
  # to click through approvals without reading them.
  #
  # Attaches no tarballs, deliberately. They are already on the registry with
  # provenance; a second copy here would be an unattested distribution channel
  # that can drift from the attested one. A link is a strictly better thing to
  # hand someone than an unsigned duplicate.
  github-release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    needs: publish
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Publish the GitHub Release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          # Explicit rather than inferred from the git remote: checkout ran
          # with persist-credentials false, and repo inference is not
          # something a release step should depend on.
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          TAG_NAME: ${{ github.ref_name }}
          PACKAGES: ${{ needs.publish.outputs.packages }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          version="${TAG_NAME#v}"

          # Unquoted on purpose: PACKAGES is a space-separated list of
          # directory names, and word-splitting it into separate arguments is
          # the intent. Every element comes from the literal package list in
          # the resolve step, so there is nothing here to re-split badly.
          # shellcheck disable=SC2086
          node ./scripts/release-notes.mjs "$version" $PACKAGES > /tmp/notes.md

          flags=(--title "$TAG_NAME" --notes-file /tmp/notes.md)
          # A prerelease must not claim the repository's "Latest release"
          # banner, for the same reason it publishes to `next` instead of
          # `latest`: it is not what a first-time reader should land on.
          # Derived from the version exactly as the dist-tag above is.
          if [[ "$version" == *-* ]]; then
            flags+=(--prerelease)
          else
            flags+=(--latest)
          fi

          # Idempotent, matching the publish loop: re-running a release that
          # partly failed has to converge instead of erroring. `gh release
          # create` fails outright when the release already exists.
          if gh release view "$TAG_NAME" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "release $TAG_NAME already exists, updating it"
            gh release edit "$TAG_NAME" "${flags[@]}"
          else
            # --verify-tag stops gh from inventing a missing tag at the
            # default branch head, which would produce a release pointing at
            # something other than what was just published.
            gh release create "$TAG_NAME" --verify-tag "${flags[@]}"
          fi
          gh release view "$TAG_NAME" --json url --jq '"✓ " + .url'

# NVIDIA Icons

Official NVIDIA GUI icon packages for web and React applications: raw SVG
assets, and React components that render via a lightweight sprite-injection
runtime. All icon path data ships in the package and is bundled at install
time; there is no CDN or web-font dependency at runtime. See
[Rendering model](#rendering-model) below for how the React components work
and their SSR caveat.

## Overview

This repository publishes four npm packages under the `@nvidia` scope:

| Package | Description |
|---|---|
| [`@nvidia/gui-icons`](./packages/gui-icons) | Raw SVG assets + TypeScript constants (748 icons, `line` and `fill` variants) |
| [`@nvidia/react-gui-icons`](./packages/react-gui-icons) | React icon components for GUI Icons (sprite-based rendering) |
| [`@nvidia/micro-gui-icons`](./packages/micro-gui-icons) | Raw SVG assets + TypeScript constants for Micro GUI Icons (24 utility icons) |
| [`@nvidia/react-micro-gui-icons`](./packages/react-micro-gui-icons) | React icon components for Micro GUI Icons (sprite-based rendering) |

## Documentation

This README and the per-package READMEs linked above are the complete
documentation today. A browsable icon gallery and searchable docs site is
planned, but is **not yet available**. Until it ships, the authoritative list
of every icon name is the `IconNames` constant exported from
`@nvidia/gui-icons` and `@nvidia/micro-gui-icons`. To browse by keyword, use
`IconTagMap` from either package; to browse by category, use `IconCategoryMap`
from `@nvidia/gui-icons` (the Micro set ships no categories, see
[Finding an icon](#finding-an-icon)).

## Getting started

```sh
# Raw SVG assets + TypeScript constants
npm install @nvidia/gui-icons

# React icon components
npm install @nvidia/react-gui-icons
```

```tsx
import { NvidiaGuiIcon } from "@nvidia/react-gui-icons";

<NvidiaGuiIcon iconName="gpu" />;
```

## Requirements

- **Node.js:** 22 or newer (`engines.node` is `>=22`).
- **React** (React packages only): `^17.0.0 || ^18.0.0 || ^19.0.0` as a peer
  dependency. The base `@nvidia/gui-icons` / `@nvidia/micro-gui-icons` packages
  have no runtime dependencies.

## Usage

### React: generic component

```tsx
import { NvidiaGuiIcon } from "@nvidia/react-gui-icons";

// line variant (default)
<NvidiaGuiIcon iconName="gpu" />

// fill variant, custom size
<NvidiaGuiIcon iconName="gpu" variant="fill" size="24px" />
```

### React: tree-shakable named imports

```tsx
// barrel import (tree-shakable by bundlers with sideEffects: false support)
import { Gpu, Add, Close } from "@nvidia/react-gui-icons/icons";

// per-icon subpath import (explicit tree-shaking boundary)
import { Gpu } from "@nvidia/react-gui-icons/icons/Gpu";

<Gpu variant="line" size="1em" />
```

These packages do **not** use `external-svg-loader`, CDN-hosted SVG files, or
web fonts. All path data is bundled at install time; see
[Rendering model](#rendering-model) for how it reaches the DOM.

### Finding an icon

There is no hosted icon browser yet, so the icon set is searchable
programmatically instead. Every name, category and keyword ships with the
package as plain data, and all of it is typed.

```ts
import {
  IconNames,        // all 748 names
  IconTagMap,       // name -> search keywords
  IconCategoryMap,  // category -> names
  getIconCategory,  // name -> category
  isIconName,       // runtime type guard
} from "@nvidia/gui-icons";

// Search by name or keyword
const matches = IconNames.filter(
  (name) => name.includes("gpu") || IconTagMap[name]?.includes("gpu"),
);
// -> ["gpu", "gpu-card", "gpu-card-multi", "gpu-card-off", "gpu-off", "gpu-sync"]

getIconCategory("gpu");             // -> "hardware"
IconCategoryMap.hardware.length;    // -> 118
isIconName("not-an-icon");          // -> false
```

`IconCategories` lists the 14 categories and `IconTags` the full keyword
vocabulary. Both are exported as `const` arrays with matching `IconCategory`
and `IconTag` types, so an editor will autocomplete them and a typo is a
compile error rather than a blank icon.

`@nvidia/micro-gui-icons` exports the same name and keyword API: `IconNames`,
`isIconName`, `IconTags`, `IconTagMap`, and the `IconName` / `IconTag` types.
It ships **no categories**. At 24 icons the set is small enough to read in one
go, so `IconCategories`, `IconCategoryMap` and `getIconCategory` exist only on
`@nvidia/gui-icons`.

The React packages re-export the `IconName` and `Variant` types for their own
icon set. They do not re-export the name, tag or category *values*; import
those from the matching base package.

### Raw SVG assets

```ts
import { IconNames, isIconName } from "@nvidia/gui-icons";

// Resolve an SVG file's URL through the package's ./assets/* subpath export
const svgUrl = import.meta.resolve("@nvidia/gui-icons/assets/line/gpu.svg");
```

`import.meta.resolve` requires Node.js or a bundler that supports it (Vite,
webpack 5+, esbuild). If your bundler doesn't, resolve the package's install
path yourself (e.g. via `require.resolve` or your bundler's asset-URL syntax)
and join it with `assets/<variant>/<name>.svg`.

SVG files are available at `assets/fill/<name>.svg` and `assets/line/<name>.svg`
within each installed package.

### Rendering model

The React components do not inline `<path>` markup directly. Each renders
`<svg><use href="#<symbolId>" /></svg>` against a `<symbol>` definition that's
injected into `document.body` the first time that icon mounts (see
`runtime/sprite.tsx` in each React package). This keeps rendered markup small
and de-duplicates repeated icons, at the cost of one extra step between mount
and paint.

**SSR / no-JS caveat:** the injection runs in `useLayoutEffect` (falling back
to `useEffect` when `document` is undefined), so server-rendered HTML and any
render that never executes React effects (static export previews, `noscript`
fallbacks) will show an empty `<svg>` with no visible icon until hydration.

If you need icons to render in the initial HTML (SSR, static generation, or
snapshot testing), render `<NvidiaGuiIconSprite />` (or
`<NvidiaMicroGuiIconSprite />`) once, high in your tree. It renders each
`<symbol>` declaratively as part of the React tree instead of via an effect,
so the symbols are present in the markup on first paint and every `<Icon />`
that references them resolves immediately.

**Pass the icons you actually use.** `getNvidiaGuiIconSpriteSymbols` accepts
icon names, or `{ iconName, variant }` objects when you need a variant other
than `line`, and returns the symbol payloads with duplicates removed:

```tsx
import {
  NvidiaGuiIcon,
  NvidiaGuiIconSprite,
  getNvidiaGuiIconSpriteSymbols,
} from "@nvidia/react-gui-icons";

// Built once at module scope: the set is static, and hoisting keeps the prop
// identity stable across renders.
const SPRITE_SYMBOLS = getNvidiaGuiIconSpriteSymbols([
  "gpu",
  "trash",
  { iconName: "gpu", variant: "fill" },
]);

function App() {
  return (
    <>
      <NvidiaGuiIconSprite symbols={SPRITE_SYMBOLS} />
      <NvidiaGuiIcon iconName="gpu" />
      <NvidiaGuiIcon iconName="gpu" variant="fill" />
    </>
  );
}
```

Omitting `symbols` renders **every** symbol the package ships: that is 748
icons × 2 variants for `@nvidia/react-gui-icons`, and 24 × 2 for
`@nvidia/react-micro-gui-icons`. Every one of them lands in the markup of
every server-rendered response, so treat the bare `<NvidiaGuiIconSprite />`
as a quick way to check the wiring rather than the form to ship.

An icon whose symbol is missing from the sprite is not an error: it renders an
empty `<svg>` in the initial HTML and fills in once its own mount-time
injection runs on the client. So a name you forget to list degrades back to
the default rendering model rather than breaking, which also means a missing
entry will not show up in a client-side test. Check the server-rendered
output, not the hydrated DOM.

`getNvidiaMicroGuiIconSpriteSymbols` and `<NvidiaMicroGuiIconSprite />` are
the same API for the Micro GUI Icons package.

**Shadow DOM caveat:** the sprite is injected into `document.body`, and an SVG
`<use href="#id">` cannot resolve a `<symbol>` across a shadow boundary. Icons
rendered inside a shadow root (a web component, or a micro-frontend that
mounts into one) therefore render as an empty `<svg>` with no error. Render
`<NvidiaGuiIconSprite />` inside the same shadow root to give those icons a
`<symbol>` they can reach.

### Line and fill variants

Every icon ships in both `line` and `fill`. For glyphs that are pure strokes
with nothing to fill (arrows, chevrons, `add`, `check`, `close`), the two
variants are deliberately identical, so `variant="fill"` renders the same
artwork as `variant="line"`. That affects 98 of the 748 GUI Icons and 19 of
the 24 Micro GUI Icons.

Both variants exist for every icon regardless, so switching a whole icon set
between them never leaves a gap, and no call site needs to special-case which
glyphs have a distinct fill.

### Micro GUI Icons

The `@nvidia/micro-gui-icons` and `@nvidia/react-micro-gui-icons` packages
follow the same API shape for the 24-icon utility set.

### Bundle size guidance

| Import style | Bundle includes | Approx. cost |
|---|---|---|
| `import { NvidiaGuiIcon }` | Full inline map, all 748 icons | 490 KB (150 KB gzipped) |
| `import { Gpu } from ".../icons"` | Only `Gpu` path data (tree-shaken by bundler) | ~1 KB |
| `import { Gpu } from ".../icons/Gpu"` | Only `Gpu` path data (explicit subpath) | ~1 KB |

Figures are for `@nvidia/react-gui-icons` at 1.0.0, measured on the built
output. The Micro GUI Icons equivalent is 8.6 KB (1.5 KB gzipped) for its full
map.

The generic `NvidiaGuiIcon` component resolves icon names at runtime, so a
bundler cannot know which icons you use and has to include all of them. Reach
for it only when icon names genuinely are dynamic. For a fixed set of icons,
which is the common case, use the named subpath imports and pay for what you
render.

## Accessibility

Every generated icon component defaults to `aria-hidden="true"` and
`focusable="false"`. Icons are treated as decorative by default, invisible to
screen readers, and excluded from the tab order.

That default is deliberate. The same icon is decorative beside a visible label
and meaningful in an icon-only button, and only the call site knows which. An
icon announced next to the label it duplicates is noise.

If an icon carries meaning on its own, give it a name with `title`:

```tsx
<NvidiaGuiIcon iconName="trash" title="Delete item" />
```

That renders a `<title>`, sets `role="img"` and drops `aria-hidden` together,
so there is no half-configured state to land in.

**Name the action, not the glyph.** Write `title="Delete item"`, not
`title="trash"`. The library knows the shape it draws; only you know what it
does here. A wrong name is worse than none: every automated audit reports it
as passing.

An empty `title=""` is treated as decorative, so a name computed at runtime can
fall back to no name rather than an empty one.

The lower-level escape hatch still works, and `aria-label` takes precedence
over `title` if you set both:

```tsx
<NvidiaGuiIcon iconName="gpu" role="img" aria-label="GPU" aria-hidden={undefined} />
```

Note that `aria-hidden` removes the whole subtree from the accessibility tree,
so setting `aria-label` while leaving `aria-hidden` in place changes nothing a
user perceives. Prefer a visible text label next to the icon over an icon-only
control where practical.

Each package versions independently, starting at `1.0.0`: icon name removals
and renamed exports are breaking changes (semver MAJOR); new icons are minor
releases. See [CHANGELOG.md](./CHANGELOG.md) for release history.
